nodes.title: Carbonyl Group Structure & IUPAC Nomenclature
points: Carbonyl group (>C=O): Carbon is sp² hybridized, planar (bond angles ≈ 120°). Strongly polar bond (Cδ⁺ − Oδ⁻) with dipole moment 2.3 to 2.8 D.
IUPAC rules: Aldehydes named as alkanals (suffix '-al', CHO is carbon-1); Ketones named as alkanones (suffix '-one'); Carboxylic acids named as alkanoic acids (suffix '-oic acid', COOH is carbon-1).
Common carbonyl compounds: Formaldehyde (methanal), Acetaldehyde (ethanal), Acetone (propan-2-one), Acetophenone (methyl phenyl ketone), Benzophenone (diphenyl ketone), Benzaldehyde.
Dicarboxylic acids: Oxalic acid (ethanedioic), Malonic acid (propanedioic), Succinic acid (butanedioic), Phthalic acid (benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid).

formulas.label: Carbonyl group hybridization and polarity
formulas.expr: >C=O: sp² hybridized carbon, trigonal planar, dipole moment μ ≈ 2.3 to 2.8 D

nodes.title: Preparation of Aldehydes & Ketones (Named Reactions)
points: 1. Rosenmund Reduction: Acyl chloride hydrogenated using H₂ over Pd/BaSO₄ poisoned with quinoline/sulfur in boiling xylene → Aldehyde + HCl.
2. Stephen Reaction: Alkane nitrile reduced with SnCl₂ + conc HCl to aldimine hydrochloride, hydrolyzed with boiling water → Aldehyde + NH₄Cl.
3. DIBAL-H Reduction: Diisobutylaluminium hydride reduces nitriles and esters selectively at −78 °C to aldehydes.
4. Etard Reaction: Toluene oxidized with chromyl chloride (CrO₂Cl₂ in CS₂) forming brown chromium complex, hydrolyzed → Benzaldehyde.
5. Gattermann-Koch Reaction: Benzene treated with CO + HCl in presence of anhydrous AlCl₃ / CuCl under high pressure → Benzaldehyde.
6. Friedel-Crafts Acylation: Benzene treated with RCOCl / anhydrous AlCl₃ → Alkyl aryl ketone (e.g. acetophenone).

formulas.label: Rosenmund reduction (acid chloride to aldehyde)
formulas.expr: R-COCl + H₂ (Pd/BaSO₄, quinoline, Δ) → R-CHO + HCl

formulas.label: Gattermann-Koch formylation of benzene
formulas.expr: C₆H₆ + CO + HCl (anhydrous AlCl₃/CuCl) → C₆H₅-CHO + HCl

nodes.title: Nucleophilic Addition Reactions of Carbonyl Compounds
points: Reactivity order: Formaldehyde > other aldehydes > ketones > bulky ketones (aldehydes are more reactive due to lesser steric hindrance and lesser +I electron donation by alkyl groups).
1. Addition of HCN: >C=O + HCN (base) ⇌ Cyanohydrin (>C(OH)CN); useful for step-up synthesis (acid hydrolysis of cyanohydrin yields α-hydroxy carboxylic acid).
2. Addition of NaHSO₃: >C=O + NaHSO₃ ⇌ Bisulfite addition compound (white crystalline solid); used for separation and purification of aldehydes and methyl ketones.
3. Addition of Alcohols: Aldehyde + 1 eq ROH (dry HCl) ⇌ Hemiacetal; + 2nd eq ROH ⇌ Acetal + H₂O. Ketone + ethylene glycol (dry HCl) ⇌ Cyclic ketal.
4. Addition of Grignard Reagents: Gives 1° alcohol (from HCHO), 2° alcohol (from RCHO), 3° alcohol (from RCOR) upon hydrolysis.

formulas.label: Reactivity towards nucleophilic addition
formulas.expr: HCHO > CH₃CHO > CH₃COCH₃ > C₆H₅COCH₃ (steric & inductive effects)

nodes.title: Addition-Elimination with Ammonia Derivatives
points: General reaction: >C=O + H₂N−Z (mild acid pH ≈ 3.5) ⇌ >C(OH)NHZ → >C=N−Z + H₂O.
1. Hydroxylamine (H₂N−OH) → Oxime (>C=N−OH).
2. Hydrazine (H₂N−NH₂) → Hydrazone (>C=N−NH₂).
3. Phenylhydrazine (H₂N−NHPh) → Phenylhydrazone (>C=N−NHPh).
4. 2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNP / Brady's reagent) → 2,4-DNP derivative (yellow, orange, or red crystalline precipitate; universal test for carbonyl group!).
5. Semicarbazide (H₂N−NH−CO−NH₂) → Semicarbazone (>C=N−NH−CO−NH₂; only the hydrazine NH₂ reacts, the amide NH₂ is deactivated by resonance).

formulas.label: Brady's reagent test for carbonyl group

nodes.title: Reduction, Oxidation & Identification Tests
points: 1. Clemmensen Reduction: >C=O + Zn−Hg + conc HCl (Δ) → >CH₂ (hydrocarbon) + H₂O (suitable for base-sensitive compounds).
2. Wolff-Kishner Reduction: >C=O + NH₂NH₂ (KOH, ethylene glycol, 453-473 K) → >CH₂ (hydrocarbon) + N₂↑ + H₂O (suitable for acid-sensitive compounds).
3. Tollens' Test (Silver Mirror): Aldehyde + Tollens' reagent [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ (alkaline) → RCOO⁻ + 2Ag↓ (bright silver mirror). Ketones do not respond.

4. Fehling's Test: Aliphatic aldehyde + Fehling's solution (equal parts Fehling A: CuSO₄ and Fehling B: alkaline Rochelle salt) → RCOO⁻ + Cu₂O↓ (red precipitate). Ketones and benzaldehyde do not reduce Fehling's.
5. Iodoform Test (Haloform Reaction): Compounds with CH₃−C=O or CH₃−CH(OH)− react with I₂ + NaOH → yellow ppt of CHI₃ (iodoform, mp 119 °C, antiseptic odor).

formulas.label: Wolff-Kishner reduction (basic medium)
formulas.expr: >C=O + NH₂NH₂ (KOH, ethylene glycol, Δ) → >CH₂ + N₂↑ + H₂O

nodes.title: Aldol Condensation & Cannizzaro Reaction
points: 1. Aldol Condensation: Requires carbonyl compound having at least one α-hydrogen atom; catalyzed by dilute alkali (dil NaOH, Ba(OH)₂).
Reaction: 2 molecules combine to form β-hydroxy aldehyde (aldol) or β-hydroxy ketone (ketol); heating eliminates water forming α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compound.
Example: 2CH₃CHO (dil NaOH) ⇌ CH₃−CH(OH)−CH₂−CHO (3-hydroxybutanal) (Δ, −H₂O) → CH₃−CH=CH−CHO (but-2-enal / crotonaldehyde).
2. Cannizzaro Reaction: Requires aldehydes having NO α-hydrogen atoms (HCHO, C₆H₅CHO, (CH₃)₃C−CHO); treated with 50% concentrated alkali.
Self-oxidation-reduction (disproportionation): One molecule is reduced to an alcohol, the other is oxidized to a carboxylic acid salt.
Cross-Cannizzaro: C₆H₅CHO + HCHO + 50% NaOH → C₆H₅CH₂OH (benzyl alcohol) + HCOONa (sodium formate; HCHO is oxidized preferentially).

nodes.title: Preparation of Carboxylic Acids
points: 1. Oxidation of 1° Alcohols & Aldehydes: Using acidified KMnO₄ / K₂Cr₂O₇ or Jones reagent (CrO₃ + H₂SO₄).

2. Oxidation of Alkylbenzenes: Toluene / ethylbenzene heated with alkaline KMnO₄ (followed by H₃O⁺) yields Benzoic acid (entire alkyl chain is oxidized provided it has at least one benzylic hydrogen; tert-butylbenzene is not oxidized).
3. Hydrolysis of Nitriles and Amides: R−CN + H₂O (H⁺) → R−CONH₂ (partial); R−CONH₂ + H₂O (H⁺, Δ) → R−COOH + NH₄⁺ (complete).
4. Carbonation of Grignard Reagent: R−MgX + CO₂ (solid dry ice, dry ether) → R−COOMgX (H₃O⁺) → R−COOH + Mg(OH)X (steps up carbon chain by 1).
5. Hydrolysis of Acyl halides & Anhydrides: RCOCl + H₂O → RCOOH + HCl; (RCO)₂O + H₂O → 2RCOOH.

formulas.label: Grignard carbonation (dry ice)
formulas.expr: R-MgX + O=C=O (dry ether) → R-COOMgX (H₃O⁺) → R-COOH + Mg(OH)X

nodes.title: Acidity of Carboxylic Acids & Chemical Reactions
points: Acidity & Resonance: Carboxylic acids are stronger acids than alcohols and phenols (RCOOH > Phenol > H₂O > ROH). Carboxylate ion (RCOO⁻) is stabilized by two equivalent resonance structures with negative charge delocalized over two electronegative oxygen atoms.
Substituent effects: Electron-withdrawing groups (−NO₂ > −CN > −F > −Cl > −Br > −I > −Ph) increase acidity via −I effect; Electron-donating groups (−CH₃, −C₂H₅) decrease acidity via +I effect.
1. Acyl Chloride formation: RCOOH + PCl₅ / PCl₃ / SOCl₂ → RCOCl.
2. Esterification: RCOOH + R'OH (conc H₂SO₄) ⇌ RCOOR' + H₂O.
3. Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) Reaction: Carboxylic acid with α-H treated with X₂ (Cl₂ or Br₂) in presence of red Phosphorus → α-halocarboxylic acid.
4. Decarboxylation: RCOONa heated with Soda lime (NaOH + CaO in 3:1 ratio, Δ) → R−H + Na₂CO₃ (reduces chain by 1 carbon).

formulas.label: Relative acidity order of substituted acetic acids
formulas.expr: F-CH₂COOH > Cl-CH₂COOH > Br-CH₂COOH > I-CH₂COOH > H-COOH > CH₃-COOH

formulas.label: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction
formulas.expr: R-CH₂-COOH + X₂ (red P, H₂O) → R-CH(X)-COOH (α-halo acid) + HX

nodes.title: High-Weightage Board Named Reactions & Distinctions
points: Named reactions checklist: Rosenmund reduction (Pd/BaSO₄), Stephen reaction (SnCl₂/HCl), Etard reaction (CrO₂Cl₂), Gattermann-Koch reaction (CO/HCl), Aldol condensation (dil NaOH, α-H required), Cannizzaro reaction (50% NaOH, no α-H), HVZ reaction (X₂/red P).

Distinguishing tests: 1) Tollens' test: Aldehydes (silver mirror) vs Ketones (no reaction); 2) Fehling's test: Aliphatic aldehydes (red Cu₂O ppt) vs Benzaldehyde/Ketones (no reaction); 3) Iodoform test: CH₃CHO and all methyl ketones CH₃COR give yellow ppt of CHI₃.
Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃) test: Carboxylic acids decompose NaHCO₃ with brisk effervescence of CO₂ gas; Phenols (except picric acid) do not give this test.

formulas.label: Sodium bicarbonate test for carboxylic acids
formulas.expr: R-COOH + NaHCO₃ → R-COONa + CO₂↑ (brisk effervescence) + H₂O

nodes.title: MHT-CET High-Speed Shortcuts & Elimination Hacks
points: TRAP 1: Iodoform test eligibility: Compound MUST contain either `CH₃−C=O` or `CH₃−CH(OH)−`. Methanol (CH₃OH) DOES NOT give iodoform; Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) DOES give iodoform. Pentan-2-one gives iodoform; Pentan-3-one DOES NOT!
TRAP 2: Fehling's test limitation: Aliphatic aldehydes reduce Fehling's, but Aromatic aldehydes (Benzaldehyde C₆H₅CHO) DO NOT reduce Fehling's solution, though they reduce Tollens' reagent!
TRAP 3: Clemmensen vs Wolff-Kishner: Acid-sensitive substrate (contains −OH, −OR, C=C) → Use Wolff-Kishner (basic). Base-sensitive substrate (contains −X, ester) → Use Clemmensen (acidic)!
TRAP 4: Cannizzaro vs Aldol: Check α-carbon. If it has ≥1 hydrogen → Aldol. If 0 hydrogen (HCHO, C₆H₅CHO, Me₃C−CHO) → Cannizzaro.
TRAP 5: Soda lime ratio: NaOH : CaO = 3 : 1 by mass. CaO keeps NaOH dry and lowers the reaction temperature.

formulas.label: MHT-CET Iodoform positive compounds checklist
formulas.expr: Positive: Ethanol, Acetaldehyde, Acetone, Propan-2-ol, Acetophenone, Pentan-2-one

formulas.label: MHT-CET Iodoform negative compounds checklist
formulas.expr: Negative: Methanol, Formaldehyde, Benzaldehyde, Benzophenone, Pentan-3-one
